## Line 411

```plato

    //==
    // # Edge collapse
    //
    // Coarsening. In a mutable remesher a collapse invalidates the indices of
    // everything around it, so collapses are done one at a time against a
    // structure that is repaired after each one. Here every candidate is judged
    // against the same mesh and the accepted ones are applied together, which
    // needs a conflict rule instead: no two accepted collapses may have ADJACENT
    // endpoints, and edges are considered in edge order. A candidate rejected this
    // pass is simply reconsidered in the next one.
    //
    // Merely forbidding a SHARED endpoint is not enough, and this is the subtle
    // part. Take two collapses whose endpoints are neighbours of one another, and
    // a triangle holding one endpoint of each plus some third vertex: after both
    // collapses that triangle, and another one just like it, become the SAME
    // triangle, and the mesh has a doubled face where it had two distinct ones.
    // Requiring the whole one-ring of each endpoint to be free rules that out, at
    // the cost of accepting fewer collapses per pass.
    //
    // On top of that, every candidate must satisfy the LINK CONDITION, which is
    // what stops a collapse from pinching the surface. It is enforced inside
    // `CollapseEdges` rather than left to callers, because it is a property of
    // contraction itself and not a policy: an edge that fails it has no correct
    // collapse. A single-edge `CollapseEdge` on such an edge therefore returns the
    // mesh unchanged.
    //
    // What is still NOT checked is fold-over: a collapse that keeps the mesh a
    // manifold can still invert a nearby triangle when the surviving position is
    // far from both endpoints. The quadric minimizer is the usual source, and a
    // caller that cares can decimate in more, smaller passes.

    // True when a vertex appears in a neighbour row.
    RowContains(row: Array<VertexIndex>, vertex: VertexIndex): Boolean
        => row.Any(n => n.Value == vertex.Value);
```
